arxiv-1908-10084.title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks
arxiv-1908-10084.creator: Nils Reimers, Iryna Gurevych
arxiv-1908-10084.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Nils Reimers, Iryna Gurevych. 2018 and RoBERTa Liu et al. 2019 has set a new state-of-the-art performance on sentence-pair regression tasks like semantic textual similarity (STS). However, it requires that both sentences are fed into the network, which causes a massive computational overhead: Finding the most similar pair in a collection of 10,000 sentences requires about 50 million inference computations (~65 hours) with BERT. The construction of BERT makes it unsuitable for semantic similarity search as well as for unsupervised tasks like clustering.

arxiv-2002-06441.title: Hyperstability of orthogonally 3-Lie homomorphism: an orthogonally fixed point approach
arxiv-2002-06441.creator: Vahid Keshavarz ∗ , Sedigheh Jahedi, Themistocles M. Rassias
arxiv-2002-06441.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Vahid Keshavarz ∗ , Sedigheh Jahedi, Themistocles M. Rassias. In this paper, by using the orthogonally fixed point method, we prove the Hyers-Ulam stability and the hyperstability of orthogonally 3-Lie homomorphisms for additive ρ \rho -functional equation in 3-Lie algebras.

arxiv-2201-09971.title: Definably Amenable Groups in Continuous Logic
arxiv-2201-09971.creator: Juan Felipe Carmona, Alf Onshuus
arxiv-2201-09971.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Juan Felipe Carmona, Alf Onshuus. We introduce the notions of definable amenability and extreme definable amenability for groups in continuous structures and conduct an extensive analysis of them, drawing parallels with the classical first-order case. We characterize both notions using fixed-point properties. We show that stable and ultracompact groups are definably amenable and prove that, for groups definable in dependent theories, definable amenability is equivalent to the existence of an f f -generic type.

arxiv-2203-14742.title: A Bayesian Approach to Modelling Biological Pattern Formation with Limited Data
arxiv-2203-14742.creator: Alexey Kazarnikov 1, Robert Scheichl 1, Heikki Haario 2 and Anna Marciniak-Czochra 1
arxiv-2203-14742.description: Abstract Understanding the mechanisms of pattern formation is one of the fundamental questions in developmental biology. Since the classic work of Alan Turing, reaction-diffusion systems have been the dominant modelling approach. Alternative models combine the dynamics of diffusing molecular signals with tissue mechanics or intracellular feedback.

arxiv-2212-04730.title: ESFRAD. FORTRAN code for calculation of QED corrections to polarized ep-scattering by the electron structure function method
arxiv-2212-04730.description: Abstract The main features of the electron structure function method for calculations of the higher order QED radiative effects to polarized deep-inelastic e ​ p ep -scattering are presented. A new FORTRAN code ESFRAD based on this method was developed.

arxiv-2511-20912.title: Analytical Approximations for Beamstrahlung at Very High Energy Electron-Positron Colliders
arxiv-2511-20912.creator: Dongxing He, Arianna Formenti, Spencer Gessner, Michael Peskin
arxiv-2511-20912.description: Abstract Among the many effects that occur in beam-beam electron-positron collisions at TeV energies, emission of hard synchrotron radiation, or beamstrahlung, has special importance. Beamstrahlung determines the energy spectrum of the most energetic electrons, positrons, and photons and supplies the initial condition for the calculation of all other QED processes.

pmc-11399807.creator: Franciely Oliveira de Andrade Santos, Caroline Souza-Santos, Adrielle Andrade Passos, Roseane Nunes de Santana Campos, Paulo Ricardo Martins-Filho, Ricardo Mario Arida, Lavínia Teixeira-Machado

pmc-11417105.title: 8-weeks aerobic exercise ameliorates cognitive deficit and mitigates ferroptosis triggered by iron overload in the prefrontal cortex of APPSwe/PSEN1dE9 mice through Xc−/GPx4 pathway
pmc-11417105.creator: Chaoyang Li, Kaiyin Cui, Xinyuan Zhu, Shufan Wang, Qing Yang, Guoliang Fang
pmc-11417105.description: BackgroundAlzheimer’s disease (AD) is a degenerative disorder of the central nervous system characterized by notable pathological features such as neurofibrillary tangles and amyloid beta deposition. Additionally, the significant iron accumulation in the brain is another important pathological hallmark of AD. Exercise can play a positive role in ameliorating AD, but the mechanism is unclear.

pmc-11430959.title: A Hierarchical Neural Network for Point Cloud Segmentation and Geometric Primitive Fitting
pmc-11430959.creator: Honghui Wan, Feiyu Zhao
pmc-11430959.description: Automated generation of geometric models from point cloud data holds significant importance in the field of computer vision and has expansive applications, such as shape modeling and object recognition. However, prevalent methods exhibit accuracy issues. In this study, we introduce a novel hierarchical neural network that utilizes recursive PointConv operations on nested subdivisions of point sets.

pmc-11438995.title: Targeting auditory verbal hallucinations in schizophrenia: effective connectivity changes induced by low-frequency rTMS
pmc-11438995.creator: Xie Yuanjun, Muzhen Guan, Tian Zhang, Chaozong Ma, Lingling Wang, Xinxin Lin, Chenxi Li, Zhongheng Wang, Ma Zhujing, Huaning Wang, Fang Peng
pmc-11438995.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Low-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) has emerged as an effective intervention for alleviating symptoms of psychiatric disorders, particularly schizophrenia characterized by persistent auditory verbal hallucinations (AVH). However, the underlying mechanism of its action remain elusive. This study employed a randomized controlled design to investigate the impact of low-frequency rTMS on the neural connectivity at the stimulate site, specifically left temporoparietal junction (TPJ), in schizophrenia patients with suffering from AVH.

pmc-11452447.title: Surgery Plays a Leading Role in Breast Cancer Treatment for Patients Aged ≥90 Years: A Large Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-11452447.creator: Massimo Ferrucci, Daniele Passeri, Francesco Milardi, Andrea Francavilla, Matteo Cagol, Mariacristina Toffanin, Giacomo Montagna, Alberto Marchet
pmc-11452447.description: BackgroundThe population aged ≥90 years is increasing worldwide, yet nearly 50% of elderly breast cancer (BC) patients receive suboptimal treatments, resulting in high rates of BC-related mortality. We analyzed clinical and survival outcomes of nonagenarian BC patients to identify effective treatment strategies.MethodsThis single-institution retrospective cohort study analyzed patients aged ≥90 years diagnosed with stage I–III BC between 2007 and 2018.

pmc-12364417.title: Exploring the Perspectives of Pediatric Health Care Providers, Youth Patients, and Caregivers on Machine Learning Suicide Risk Classification: Mixed Methods Study
pmc-12364417.creator: Rohan R Dayal, Pua Lani Yang, Laura Nicole Sisson, Mira Bajaj, Shannon Archuleta, Sophie Yao, Daniel H Park, Hanae Fujii-Rios, Emily E Haroz, Andrew Coristine
pmc-12364417.description: BackgroundSuicide was the second leading cause of death for youth aged between 10 and 24 years in 2023, necessitating improved risk identification to better identify those in need of support. While machine learning (ML) applied to electronic health records shows promise in improving risk identification, further research on the perspectives of these tools is needed to better inform implementation strategies.

pmc-12481057.title: Iatrogenic migration from a multiple filler injections for tear trough: A case report
pmc-12481057.creator: Weidong Zhang, Yong Pan
pmc-12481057.description: Introduction and importanceIatrogenic migration of dermal fillers in the periorbital region represents a rare yet significant complication. Accurate assessment of patient history, imaging, and anatomical knowledge is crucial for achieving optimal outcomes. This report underscores the importance of comprehensive evaluation and tailored surgical intervention when confronted with persistent lower eyelid swelling resistant to conventional enzymatic therapy.

pmc-12592506.title: A gender comparison based network analysis for social media addiction behaviors in cross-cultural contexts
pmc-12592506.creator: Linying Li, Xiaoxiao Yuan, Luzi Lin, Antong Xiao, Yi Chen, Yu Xia, Xiang Huang
pmc-12592506.description: Social media addiction (SMA) has become a prevalent behavioral addiction among university students worldwide, with acculturation stress and social identity threats amplifying this phenomenon among international students. Prior research has focused on causal factors influencing the SMA, such as social norms and cognitive‒behavioral mechanisms, while overlooking the core features and gender differences in SMA manifestations.

pmc-12662805.title: Clinical Profiles and In‐Hospital Outcomes of Pre‐Existing Versus Newly Diagnosed Atrial Fibrillation in Coronary Care Units: Insights From the MORCOR‐TURK National Registry
pmc-12662805.creator: Ertan Aydin, Muhammed Mürsel Öğütveren, Gurbet Özge Mert, Mehtap Yeni, Sevil Gülaşti, Uğur Küçük, Başar Candemir, İbrahim Halil Tanboğa, Aymet Seyda Yilmaz

pmc-12754366.title: My Diabetes & Me: study protocol for a randomised controlled trial to test the clinical and cost-effectiveness of a diabetes self-management education programme for adults with intellectual disabilities.
pmc-12754366.creator: Laurence Taggart, Gary McDermott, Alison Dunkley, Maria Truesdale, Vivien Coates, Kamlesh Khunti, Mike Clarke, Dan Pollard, Alan Brennan, Michelle Hadjiconstantinou, Molly Caba, Colette Jackson, Aimee Anderson Smyth, Cliona McDowell, Ashley Agus, Sorcha Toase, Janet Schofield, Rosie Kelly, Tshifhiwa
pmc-12754366.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundInternational guidelines recommend structured diabetes education to empower individuals with type 2 diabetes (T2D). While DESMOND is an effective programme for T2D management, it is often inaccessible to people with intellectual disabilities (ID) due to their unique needs. There is limited evidence on the effectiveness of adapted T2D education for this group, despite the importance of tailored support in preventing complications and early mortality.We previously adapted the DESMOND programme for adults with ID, creating DESMOND-ID.

pmc-12996797.title: Multi-layered metabolic remodeling of Pseudomonas putida for efficient conversion of lignocellulosic sugars to the precursors of advanced aviation fuel
pmc-12996797.creator: Chae Won Kang, David N Carruthers, Joshua McCauley, Yan Chen, Jennifer W Gin, Christopher J Petzold, Blake A Simmons, Taek Soon Lee
pmc-12996797.description: Isoprenyl acetate, a volatile ester derived from isoprenol, is a key biosynthetic intermediate for the advanced aviation fuel candidate, 1,4-dimethylcyclooctane. Here, we engineered Pseudomonas putida KT2440 for the production of isoprenyl acetate from mixed sugar substrates. We first generated isoprenyl acetate by introducing a heterologous alcohol acetyltransferase (ATF1) and deleting three promiscuous native esterases to reduce product degradation.

pmc-13237532.title: An Explainable AI Tool (FibroX) for Detecting Advanced Liver Fibrosis in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: Protocol for a Pilot Crossover Trial
pmc-13237532.creator: Basile Njei, Ulrick Sidney Kanmounye, Amy Schwartz, Xiaolong Liang, Gotaro Toda
pmc-13237532.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundMetabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease is highly prevalent in adults with type 2 diabetes, and advanced fibrosis is its strongest prognostic marker. pmc-13624442.title: Analysis of clinical and heart rate variability parameters associated with single-vessel and multivessel coronary artery disease: A retrospective study
pmc-13624442.creator: Mingfang Zhu, Sixin Xie, Gang Lv, Xiang Zhang, Ding Peng
pmc-13624442.description: Objectives:To compare heart rate variability (HRV) parameters and cardiac biomarkers between patients with single-vessel and multivessel coronary artery disease (CAD) and assess their associations with multivessel involvement.Methodology:This retrospective study included 196 patients with angiographically confirmed CAD admitted between September 2022 and May 2025 at Ningguo People’s Hospital. Patients were classified as having single-vessel (n=55) or multivessel (n=141) disease.

pmc-13714895.title: Radial Head Fractures Cluster in the Anterolateral and Anteromedial Quadrants and Do Not Correlate With Coronoid Fracture Types
pmc-13714895.creator: Nadia Azib, Huub H. de Klerk, Job N. Doornberg, Nadalini Nettuno, Michel P. J. van den Bekerom, Neal C. Chen, Abhiram R. Bhashyam
pmc-13714895.description: BackgroundCombined radial head and coronoid fractures, including terrible triad injuries, are challenging patterns associated with elbow instability, poor clinical outcomes, and other complications. While both radial head and coronoid fractures contribute to joint stability, the relationship between their fracture morphologies remains poorly understood. Clarifying these associations may aid in preoperative planning and guide surgical decision-making for restoring elbow stability.
